newsitem.title: USA: Barney's gets $240 million buyout offer from Dickson.
newsitem.headline: Barney's gets $240 million buyout offer from Dickson.

text.p: Barney's Inc., the luxury retailer trying to reorganize in bankruptcy proceedings, Friday received a $240 million buyout proposal from Dickson Concepts (International) Ltd.

Hong Kong-based Dickson, which owns store chains worldwide, said the offer would pay the owners of Barneys New York $240 million in cash and a minority interest in Barney's future income from stores licensed outside the United States.
Barney's said it had not yet reviewed the proposal but has held talks with Dickson and its representatives regarding parts of a potential investment.
It said it did not receive Dickson's formal takeover proposal until early Friday and has not had a chance to review the offer with its financial and legal advisers.
Barney's said it has been in talks with potential investors as part of its efforts to develop a reorganization plan. It emphasised that it retains the exclusive right to file such a plan.

Saks Fifth Avenue and Neiman Marcus have also expressed interest in Barney's, according to the trade newspaper Women's Wear Daily. Any potential partner would likely seek a controlling interest in the chain, it added.
Barney's, one of the leading upscale retailers of men's and women's wear in the United States, reported total sales of $366 million for the 53 weeks to Aug. 3, 1996.

It has been operating in Chapter 11 bankruptcy since January, 1996. It said in January it had received an extension until May 5 from a U.S. bankruptcy court judge to file a reorganization plan. In Chapter 11 a company is protected from its creditors as it tries to work out a plan to pay its debts.
Once catering to the middle-class men's wear customer, Barney's in the last two decades has changed direction under the influence of the grandsons of founder Barney Pressman.

With a dramatic growth plan, Barney's moved from mid-priced to high-priced merchandise, opened women's departments and expanded into housewares and other items at luxury prices. It now operates 15 stores in the United States and two in Japan.
Barney's moved many operations from its original flagship property in New York City's Chelsea neighbourhood to a tonier address on Madison Avenue, with neighbours such as Valentino and Versace.
Dickson, based in Hong Kong, owns 270 retailers worldwide, including Harvey Nichols in London and S.T. Dupont in Paris.
"Barney's represents a unique opportunity for the group to establish a meaningful business presence in the United States," Dickson Chairman Dickson Poon said in Hong Kong.
He said the group would be able to fund the deal. "Our cash position is approxminately HK$1.3 billion ($168 million)," he said but did not detail the funding plan.
Barney's is awaiting a ruling from bankruptcy court, expected on Monday, on whether Isetan Co. Ltd., a Japanese company, is its landlord or its equity partner.
Also at stake is the future of royalty payments Barney's claims it is owed by Isetan on a license agreement Barney's claims it terminated in September 1996, Women's Wear said.
Analysts were mixed about Dickson's proposal.

"Our view on the news is positive, since Dickson has a good track record in turning around loss-making companies and the brand of Barney's is not bad and there is a good chance that they can also be successful this time," a European financial analyst said.
Dickson's Poon said the offer of minority interest in the future non-U.S. store licensing income made the bid more attractive, but he did not specify its value.
